Imnah
IM-nah
n. (proper name; firstborn of Asher; also a Levite)
Hebrew Yimnah, prosperity or he assigns, from manah, to number, to allot; the same name as Jimnah and Jimna.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Imnah is the firstborn of Asher, and the name of a Levite in Hezekiah's day. “The sons of Asher; Imnah, and Isuah, and Ishuai, and Beriah, and Serah their sister” (1 Chronicles 7:30). Genesis spells him Jimnah: “And the sons of Asher; Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister” (Genesis 46:17); Numbers gives the clan, “of Jimna, the family of the Jimnites” (Numbers 26:44). One man stands behind all three spellings. He went down into Egypt with Jacob and became the head of a family in Israel. The second Imnah was a Levite whose son served in Hezekiah's reformation: “And Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the porter toward the east, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute the oblations of the LORD, and the most holy things” (2 Chronicles 31:14). The first Imnah founded a family; the second raised a son trusted with the holy things. The name means he numbers, and God numbered both.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Imnah is a Hebrew proper name and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Imnah is a Hebrew proper name; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

The name appears in 1 Chronicles 7:30 and 2 Chronicles 31:14.

Imnah son of Asher is Jimnah in Genesis 46:17 and Jimna in Numbers 26:44.

Another Imnah was a Levite, father of Kore.

The name may mean he numbers or allots.

Key Scripture

1Ch 7:30 — "The sons of Asher; Imnah, and Isuah, and Ishuai, and Beriah, and Serah their sister."

Gen 46:17 — "And the sons of Asher; Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah, and Serah their sister: and the sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel."

Num 26:44 — "Of the children of Asher after their families: of Jimna, the family of the Jimnites: of Jesui, the family of the Jesuites: of Beriah, the family of the Beriites."

2Ch 31:14 — "And Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the porter toward the east, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute the oblations of the LORD, and the most holy things."

Modern Corruption

Spelling variants are taken as proof of contradiction; Imnah, Jimnah and Jimna are one son of Asher.

expand to see more

Critics point to variant spellings across Genesis, Numbers and Chronicles as evidence of careless or contradictory sources. Names were transliterated and pronounced differently across centuries, as English names are today. The variants confirm the same man, not different traditions.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God numbers His people by name. “All these were the children of Asher, heads of their father's house, choice and mighty men of valour” (1 Chronicles 7:40).
